notes: The original diagnosis states D. anastrepta and D. megathura have strikingly similar corollas; the 1984 Racemosae grouping places both in Group 4. Direct morphology shows unlike stamens with greatly reduced anticous anthers and larger fertile posticous anthers, so the strict heteranthery-absence gate fails.

Manning & Brothers describe D. purpurea as closely related to D. anastrepta. Direct morphology records unlike stamens, reduced/sterile anticous anthers and larger green-pollen posticous anthers, so the negative-architecture gate fails.

Direct morphology explicitly describes four equal stamens. Manning & Brothers directly observed Rediviva oil foraging with pollen deposited on the bee sternum. Biological eligibility passes, but relative closest-eligible proximity to D. anastrepta is not source-closed.

The revision describes one undivided projecting stamen set with equal filament/anther dimensions and yellow pollen; no discrete fertile stamen cohorts are described. Rediviva oil foraging and sternotribic pollen placement are directly observed. Relative closest-eligible proximity remains unresolved.

The revision describes one erect coherent stamen set with common filament/anther dimensions and yellow pollen; no discrete fertile cohorts are described. Rediviva oil foraging and facial pollen placement are directly observed. Relative closest-eligible proximity remains unresolved.

Although all anthers are alike and produce grey-green pollen, the source explicitly calls the stamens unalike: anticous and posticous fertile pairs differ in orientation and filament length. Under the frozen strict morphology gate this is not an absence control.
